title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across conditions) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Importantly, the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition executed here. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation introduces operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior surveys and empirical reports document LLM feasibility for draft configurations while stressing the need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts bounded automated repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. Such pipelines reduce mechanically checkable error classes (syntax, ordering, local-policy violations) but it remains unclear how large the marginal verifier/repair benefit is when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes. 

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment designed to isolate that marginal effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation per intent reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we measured the verifier-detected difference between accepting the candidate (baseline) and submitting it to deterministic validation with up to one automated repair (guarded). The design therefore isolates only validator-and-repair effects on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition and archive complete execution, validator traces, repair traces, reconciliation, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Work applying LLMs to NetOps and intent-driven configuration generation shows consistent feasibility in controlled or emulation settings but emphasizes verification needs [1],[2],[3]. Deterministic network verification tools and formal-analysis approaches (e.g., header-space analysis, Batfish evolution) are mature methods for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[5]. Generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows have been shown to increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, though deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [6]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats further motivate filtering and validation layers but show adaptive adversaries remain an open operational threat [7].

This study differs from prior work in three ways: (i) it uses a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the validator/repair marginal effect on identical candidates; (ii) it reports deterministic provider-call reconciliation that maps model stages (shared initial generation, repair) to accounting; and (iii) it archives full validator traces, repair traces, and analysis manifests so numeric outcomes are auditable from the evidence bundle.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion and contamination detectors, the primary tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), the model-call budget, and the analysis executor. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a7... (referenced in the Disclosure Statement).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. By design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. Provider-call accounting recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, reconciling to 250 shared initial generations plus a single repair call during execution.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Representative tasks exercised workflow constraints (make-before-break switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. The full task manifest and representative payloads are archived in the evidence bundle.

Model invocation, guarded pipeline, validator, and repair. The declared model for initial generation was gpt-5-mini. Each shared candidate was scored by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation: CLI parsing, command-count checks, required_sequence ordering, workflow-constraint checks, and a snapshot comparison between the validator-derived final_state and the task expected_final_state. For guarded episodes, if valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one deterministic template-driven repair constrained to syntactic and ordering fixes (reorder commands to match required_sequence, split/join tokens, correct obvious token ordering), then re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration or human escalation was permitted by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items that failed vendor-parsers preventing verification, or that contained credential-like tokens or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens or private-address artifacts; flagged items would be excluded from primary analysis and reported. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged: complete_pair_count = 250 and contamination_summary is empty.

Analysis. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on the paired outcomes. We also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap parameters) are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.results:
Execution and basic accounting. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call auditing reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call (stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}). No episodes were excluded and no contamination flags were raised.

Primary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the only repair call exercised; that repair converted the failing baseline candidate into a guarded-pass. The observed repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) is p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These values and associated analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle.

Validator diagnostics and representative artifacts. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count and required_command_count matching the task required_sequence. Representative scoring artifacts (for example, task-000003) show parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, and valid = true in both baseline and guarded episodes. Representative raw responses, normalized configurations, and validator traces are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. In this preregistered, shared_initial_candidate experiment on constrained emulation-style tasks, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of adding deterministic validation plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the lone failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under the executed pipeline and task scope.

Why the observed gain was small. Artifact-grounded factors that explain the small observed guarded gain include: (1) constrained task design and deterministic task generator reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced syntactically consistent candidates for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checked mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) but does not cover broader behavioral correctness, vendor runtime behaviors, or emergent multi-device interactions.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 percentage-point effect with ~80% power; the realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently, the paired-bootstrap CI and the observed contingency provide the most practically informative characterization of the verifier-marginal effect under these conditions.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results are specific to the exact prompt templates, single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics used. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol-level correctness. External validity: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain open threats.

Operational framing and implications. These findings show that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the measured marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This result does not imply validators and repairs are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts: validator scope, multi-iteration repair policies, human escalation, production heterogeneity, and adversarial threats can materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. On N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the sole failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All run artifacts and manifests referenced below are archived in the study evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode as specified in the preregistration. Execution manifest reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) and stage_counts {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Preregistration and immutable prompt references (archived): preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Evidence-bundle pointer: the full execution and analysis manifest and archived artifacts (raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, task manifest, provider audit, and analysis CSVs) are contained in the study evidence bundle; the archived full manifest is available as execution/execution_manifest.json within that bundle (see preregistration SHA above and the archived manifest for file-level hashes). This Disclosure intentionally omits per-file bookkeeping and long lists of individual file hashes from the paper body; full file-level manifests and hashes are included in the archived evidence bundle for auditability.

Executed confirmatory estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
